analysis.title: markets / macro (Tony Pasquariello, 7 Nov 2026)
key_insights: Pasquariello says 2026 has been a year of distinct regimes, and the second half differs sharply from the first. Momentum factor has had an immense drawdown over the past five months after a strong start.
Q2'26 may have marked the peak of the rally for US equities, with the SOX doubling intra-quarter. Since then conditions have become much harder, and this week was one of the most savage he has seen.
He frames US equities through three factors: earnings growth, flow of capital and the AI narrative.
Earnings growth was 33% in Q2 and Q3 is tracking at 35%, the fastest pace outside post-recession recoveries in over 30 years. Growth is set to slow, and the market keys off the rate of change.

If S&P EPS grows 18% next year, history still favors the bulls. If nominal growth stays above trend, earnings growth should stay strong and give ballast to the market. The GS forecast is very sensitive to AI capex, and risks to it rose this week.
He finds it increasingly hard to see earnings delivering the same upward convexity as in recent years.

The market has absorbed broad liquidation for three months, concentrated this week in global AI stocks. Hedge funds have sold non-stop since mid-August, taking net exposure across the GS PB book to its lowest since March.
Households' demand turned down toward the end of summer, with pockets of net selling this week. Corporate buybacks are constrained while large financings have cleared the market.
He expects flows to be more favorable over the last eight weeks of 2026, but worries 2027 will see the largest increase in net supply since 2000.

Consensus has big-five AI capex growth slowing from 96% this year to 44% next year, and the market was uncomfortable with hyperscalers moving deeper into negative free cash flow. This week's news is arguably better for hyperscalers but worse for the rest of the AI infrastructure complex.
He sees less upside convexity in the picks-and-shovels part of the AI trade. If the news slows the buildout and lengthens the cycle, medium-term optimism on the theme can be retained.

Conclusion: the primary trend remains intact and he expects one last push higher in the S&P before the turn, with 2027 a less rewarding year. He expects the base level of index volatility to rise and the environment to favor flexible traders.
Healthcare is quietly the second best performing sector YTD, from defensive macro, strong EPS and flow of funds. He will return to it next week.
He calls the market fairly valued: NDX and SOX trade on forward multiples about 4 turns lower than just before late November 2022.
Two people he respects say equities are too sanguine relative to credit, and he invites views on it.
The TMT momentum pair has lost two-thirds of its value since the June highs and is now down on the year.

sector_views.rationale: Second best performing sector YTD, driven by defensive macro positioning, strong EPS and flow of funds. He plans to follow up next week.
He sees less upside convexity as the buildout intensity is questioned, though hyperscalers may fare better.

tension_points.bull_case: If nominal GDP growth stays very strong, earnings growth should stay well above trend, and 18% S&P EPS growth next year still favors bulls. The market is now fairly valued.
tension_points.bear_case: The market keys off the rate of change, growth is set to slow, flows are worsening, and the AI buildout is at more risk than at any point in four years.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sustained slowdown in AI capex or in nominal GDP growth, which the GS forecast is very sensitive to.

tension_points.bull_case: News this week may lengthen the buildout cycle, which keeps medium-term optimism on the theme and is arguably better for hyperscalers.
tension_points.bear_case: Less upside convexity in picks-and-shovels names, more left tails, and hyperscalers pushing deeper into negative free cash flow.
